description:
Company Description

Givebutter is the most-loved nonprofit fundraising and CRM platform, empowering millions of changemakers to raise more, pay less, and give better. Nonprofits use Givebutter to replace multiple tools so they can launch fundraisers and events, use donation forms and donor management (CRM), send emails and text blasts—all in one place. Use of the Givebutter platform is completely free with a 100% transparent tip-or-fee model.

Givebutter has been certified as a Great Place to Work® every year since 2021, and is the #1 rated nonprofit software company on G2 across multiple categories.

Our mission is to empower the changemaker in all of us. We believe giving should be fun, so you’ll want to do it again, and we also believe that work should be fun, so that you’ll have the greatest impact. We are excited to hear from talented people who want to work with other talented people in making the world a butter place—and have fun along the way. 

Role Description

The Director of Revenue Operations sets the strategy, systems, and operating standards that enable Givebutter's revenue organization to run on a single connected system and a single trusted set of numbers. You'll own Revenue Operations across Sales, Customer Experience, and Marketing, and build and lead the team that delivers it. This is a strategy and team-building role, not a hands-on admin or ticket-queue role: you set direction, standards, and priorities, then give your team clear ownership and the decision rights to execute.

You'll report to the Vice President of Sales and serve as a strategic partner to GTM leadership. You make and document decisions within the RevOps scope and provide clear, time-bound recommendations for decisions that require executive approval. Success looks like accurate forecasts, data leaders trust, GTM processes that scale without added friction, and a RevOps team that moves quickly because it is empowered to own its work. Done well, this role helps Givebutter's revenue teams spend less time fighting their tools and more time helping nonprofits raise more.

We want to hear from people who…

  • Systems Thinking & Process Design: Sets the RevOps systems strategy and roadmap across GTM; owns tech stack decisions and budget. Builds and leads a team that designs architecture supporting long-term revenue goals.

  • Data Accuracy & Insight Generation: Owns the GTM data model, forecasting process, and KPI framework; ensures leaders work from one source of truth. Partners with Finance and Data on revenue planning, targets, and bonus and incentive tracking.

  • Cross-Functional Alignment: Serves as a strategic partner to the VP of Sales and GTM leadership; leads GTM planning cycles and operating rhythms. Sets clear ownership boundaries between functions and holds partners accountable for shared outcomes.

  • Technical and Operational Problem-Solving: Defines operational resilience strategy for GTM systems; eliminates major failure points before they impact revenue. Makes clear, timely decisions on complex trade-offs and empowers the team to own resolution.

  • Continuous Improvement & Enablement: Defines the RevOps enablement strategy and operating standards across GTM; measures the impact of process changes. Builds a team culture of continuous improvement, learning, and accountability.

Responsibilities

  • Set and own the Revenue Operations strategy and roadmap across Sales, Customer Experience, and Marketing. Make and document decisions within the RevOps scope, including the GTM tech stack and the RevOps budget, and provide the VP of Sales with clear, time-bound recommendations for decisions that require executive approval.

  • Build, lead, and develop the RevOps team. Hire and coach for growth; assign clear ownership of systems, reporting, and request intake; and delegate decision rights so work moves without routing through a single approver.

  • Own the GTM systems architecture, with HubSpot as the source of truth for revenue data. Ensure CRM, integrations, and GTM tooling work as one connected system, and lead evaluation, implementation, and governance of new tools.

  • Own the GTM data model, KPI framework, and forecasting process. Partner with the Data team on data infrastructure and with Finance on revenue targets, so GTM leaders can plan and make decisions from a single source of truth.

  • Lead revenue planning workstreams, including annual planning, quota setting and attainment tracking, RevOps budget management, and spend tracking, in partnership with Finance and GTM leadership.

  • Own the tracking and calculation of revenue bonus and incentive payouts. Partner with Finance and People on plan mechanics, payout accuracy, and clear communication to plan participants.

  • Build predictive analytics and performance reporting that show the downstream impact of sales and marketing investments. Translate trends, risks, and opportunities into clear recommendations for the VP of Sales and GTM leaders.

  • Lead GTM operating rhythms, including forecast reviews and planning cycles. Set clear ownership boundaries for handoffs from lead to closed deal to onboarding and ongoing customer success, and hold partner teams accountable for shared outcomes.

  • Define the RevOps enablement and change-management approach for new systems, workflows, and governance. Measure adoption and the impact of process changes, and retire what isn't working.

Requirements

  • 8+ years of experience in Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, or GTM Operations, including 3+ years leading a team.

  • Proven track record of owning GTM systems strategy and administration in HubSpot or a comparable CRM at a growth-stage company.

  • Demonstrated ownership of forecasting, KPI frameworks, and revenue planning (annual planning, quota setting, and budget) that executive leaders relied on.

  • Demonstrated ability to build and develop a team by delegating ownership, setting clear decision rights, and growing team members into independent owners of their work.

  • Experience leading cross-functional change across Sales, Customer Experience, and Marketing, from system design through adoption.

  • Or equivalent combination of relevant experience and demonstrated competency in the above areas.

  • Experience building or scaling a RevOps function through a reporting-line or operating-model change.

  • Experience administering sales incentive and bonus plans in partnership with Finance.

  • Experience with a hybrid product-led and sales-led SaaS motion.

  • Familiarity with nonprofit technology or mission-driven software environments.

More about Givebutter

Benefits

  • Remote Work: Work remotely from one of our 10 hubs (Austin, Denver, Indianapolis, Los Angeles, San Francisco, New York, Salt Lake City, Minneapolis, Seattle, and Nashville).

  • Health Insurance: We offer Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance covered 100% for employees as well as HSA and FSA accounts.

  • Dependent Care Coverage: We offer coverage for dependents, with 50% of Medical, Dental, and Vision premiums covered for all eligible dependents.

  • Mental Health: Givebutter health insurance plans come with access to a TalkSpace membership.

  • 401k: We offer a 3% 401k match for all eligible employee's.

  • Vacation and Holidays: Givebutter offers a Flexible PTO policy with uncapped vacation days and company-recognized holidays.

  • Wellness Week: Givebutter closes for one week each summer to prioritize rest and recharge for the entire team.

  • Parental Leave: We offer 12 weeks of paid leave for all parents and comprehensive leave planning management through Aidora.

  • Family Care Support: Access a company-paid UrbanSitter membership plus care credits to book trusted, background-checked caregivers for childcare, senior care, pet care, and household support when you need it most.

  • Home Office Stipend: Upgrade your home office with company-sponsored expenses, including high-quality laptops, monitors, and modern technology.

  • Coworking Stipend: Enjoy a monthly stipend that gives you the freedom to work from coworking spaces or cafés whenever you need connection, community, or a change of scenery.

  • Charitable Giving: Employees are encouraged to donate up to $50/month to any verified nonprofit they wish to support on Givebutter.

  • Professional Development: We offer learning and development reimbursement opportunities.

  • Love What You Do: We are a mission-driven company serving the charitable sector. Feel good about the work you're doing and the company you work for.

Interview Process

Below is a high-level outline of our standard interview process

  1. Recruiter Screen: A 30-minute conversation to learn more about your background, walk through the role, and ensure mutual alignment on expectations, values, and logistics.

  2. Hiring Manager Interview: A deeper dive into your relevant experience, skillset, and working style. This is your first opportunity to connect directly with the person who may be your future manager.

  3. Assessment (technical or non-technical): This stage will vary based on the role. It could involve a live coding session, case study, or take-home project. Some roles may include two parts to this stage to evaluate both practical skills and problem-solving approaches

  4. Values Interview: A conversation with team members focused on how you align with our core values and leadership principles.

  5. References: We connect with a few folks you’ve worked closely with to get a better picture of your working style and impact.

  6. Offer: If all goes well, we’ll move to the offer stage!

Please note, we will have an AI note-taking tool join most of our interviews.

Hi potential new butterslice! A recent study from LinkedIn showed that most women apply to jobs only when they meet 100% of the requirements, whereas men will hit the apply button if they hit 60%. Givebutter is committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. So to the women and nonbinary folks out there feeling unsure if you're a perfect fit, we strongly encourage you to apply!
